key_insight: Boron doping stabilizes mixed-valence Cu-O phases, widening the low-resistivity window and suppressing early conversion to CuO as oxygen partial pressure increases.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tunable sputtered Cu-O route to lower-resistance oxide layers that could improve transparent electrodes and hole-transport materials in optoelectronic and photovoltaic devices.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Cu-O thin films with controlled boron incorporation
Systematic variation of oxygen partial pressure to map phase evolution
Phase, bonding, and electrical characterization versus processing conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a clear Cu2O → Cu2O/Cu4O3 → CuO transition with increasing oxygen partial pressure, while highly B-doped films retain Cu4O3 under oxygen-rich conditions and reach resistivity near 0.06 Ω·cm.
watch_item: Stabilizing mixed-valence phases may depend sensitively on deposition conditions, so process reproducibility and long-term phase stability still need validation.
paper_title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu-O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
